args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all three regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and look into why it was promoted even though staging was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer was paged. It says what failed, what I did, and that the service has recovered. Its next steps are to find the cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying and to work out how it was promoted.

The test build of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging but went to production anyway. That's worth checking in the follow-up.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
